go?</h1><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p style="text-align: justify;"><br></p><p style="text-align: justify;"><br></p><p style="text-align: justify;"><br></p><p style="text-align: justify;">Tools implemented under MCP servers are functions that return pydantic objects to the orchestrator MCP server which can provide this data as input to other tools. The exception to this rule is article contents which is stored in an SQLite database by the collector MCP server so as not to overwelm the context window of the llm powering the MCP client.</p><p style="text-align: justify;"><br></p><h1 style="margin-top: 0px;">So what do we have in the end?</h1><div><span style="text-align: justify;">The final thing that the orchestrator will do is to call a tool (technically an mcp prompt not a tool) implemented under the analyst MCP server that will prompt the orchestrator MCP client to form the final report from information in its context window. This context window will include any data that the MCP servers have returned from functions:</span></div><p>A collection of events from the last 24 hours, where each event has listed:</p><p></p><ul><li><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">The impact on each of our 4 sections including score and justification</span></li><li><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">The name of any actors involved&nbsp;</span></li><li><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">Relavant theme tags</span></li><li><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">The source article headlines and metadata sutch as source</span></li></ul><p></p><div>A collection of claims from the last 24 hours with some agreement and variance scores</div><div><br></div><div>A collection of actors from the last 24 hours with analysis of each actor</div><div><br></div><div style="text-align: right;">...as well as many intermediate values which are largely subsets of the above datastructures</div><div style="text-align: right;"><br></div><div><div><span style="text-align: justify;"><br></span></div><div><span style="text-align: justify;">This does <b>not </b>include the article body of the articles as that is never returned from the collector MCP server (so hopefully no direct plagerism is possible).</span></div></div><div><span style="text-align: justify;"><br></span></div><p style="text-align: justify;"><br></p>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="810" width="515" x="15" y="20" div.h1: What does the MCP architecture do exactly?
div.p: Each of the 3 MCP servers provide tools to the orchestrator MCP client. This orchestrator has the ability to use any of the tools as and when it chooses however, in our case we give the orchestrator a system prompt telling it to call each tool sequencially forming a dataprocessing pipeline of articles into events, actors and themes before summaring the results.

div.h1: Where does all the data go?
div.p: Tools implemented under MCP servers are functions that return pydantic objects to the orchestrator MCP server which can provide this data as input to other tools. The exception to this rule is article contents which is stored in an SQLite database by the collector MCP server so as not to overwelm the context window of the llm powering the MCP client.
div.h1: So what do we have in the end?

div.span: The final thing that the orchestrator will do is to call a tool (technically an mcp prompt not a tool) implemented under the analyst MCP server that will prompt the orchestrator MCP client to form the final report from information in its context window. This context window will include any data that the MCP servers have returned from functions:

div.p: A collection of events from the last 24 hours, where each event has listed:

li.span: The impact on each of our 4 sections including score and justification
The name of any actors involved
The source article headlines and metadata sutch as source

div.div: A collection of claims from the last 24 hours with some agreement and variance scores
A collection of actors from the last 24 hours with analysis of each actor

div.style: text-align: right;

div.div: ...as well as many intermediate values which are largely subsets of the above datastructures

div.style: text-align: right;

div.span: This does not include the article body of the articles as that is never returned from the collector MCP server (so hopefully no direct plagerism is possible).

MPs think Starmer should face inquiry into whether he misled them on Mandelson vetting
'. The opinion value indicates how much an article holds this to be the case.
